item.title: GRAIL Launches Digital Data Pipeline for Humanoid Robot Manipulation Training
item.description:
GRAIL Launches Digital Data Pipeline for Humanoid Robot Manipulation Training

🔍 Overview

GRAIL is a fully digital data-generation pipeline for humanoid loco-manipulation.

It composes 3D assets, simulator-ready scenes, robot-proportioned characters, and video foundation model priors to synthesize metric 4D human-object interaction (HOI) trajectories, then retargets them to a Unitree G1 and trains task-general policies for pick-up, whole-body manipulation, sitting, and terrain traversal.

🧩 How it works

The pipeline generates synthetic 4D human-object interaction trajectories using composed 3D assets and video foundation model priors, then retargets these to a Unitree G1 robot for policy training.

⚙️ Key details

  • Uses only GRAIL-generated data for training
  • Supports tasks: pick-up, whole-body manipulation, sitting, and terrain traversal
  • Policies transfer to real-world object pick-up and stair-climbing
  • Requires Linux GPU host with NVIDIA-enabled Docker
  • Examples include input videos in the GRAIL repository root
  • Two provider options: Kling (standard image) and MiniMax-H3 (nvgrail/grail:1.2.0-minimax-h3)
Component Description
3D Assets Composed with simulator-ready scenes
Video Priors Foundation model priors for interaction synthesis
Robot Unitree G1 for retargeting
Training Tasks Pick-up, whole-body manipulation, sitting, terrain traversal

🚀 Availability

  • Start in the GRAIL repository root on a Linux GPU host with NVIDIA-enabled Docker
  • Require Git LFS assets and reconstruction/retargeting submodules
  • Install guide available at docs/source/installation.md
  • First setup provisions workers in mounted checkout and cache
  • Robot stage needs SOMA Retargeter checkout, robot Python, and G1 assets
  • Retargeting setup documented at docs/source/installation.md#soma-retargeter-unitree-g1--dex3

💡 Why it matters

Using only GRAIL-generated data, the resulting egocentric visual policies transfer to real-world object pick-up and stair-climbing, demonstrating the pipeline’s effectiveness for real-world robot skill transfer.

#Robotics #Simulation #Humanoid #GRAIL #DataGeneration

Source: NVlabs/GRAIL

item.title: ReLoco Unifies Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery in Single Policy
item.description:
ReLoco Unifies Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery in Single Policy

A new framework called ReLoco enables humanoid robots to walk, run, recover from falls, and resume commanded motion using a single proprioceptive policy without controller switching or on-robot fine-tuning. The approach was validated on the 64.5-kg Tiangong 3.0 humanoid platform.

🔍 Overview

  • Paper title: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors
  • Submission date: 18 Nov 2026
  • Domain: Computer Science > Robotics
  • Core contribution: One policy handles locomotion, get-up from arbitrary fallen postures, and command resumption
  • Deployment platform: 64.5-kg Tiangong 3.0 humanoid

🧩 How it works

  • Uses behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors to learn diverse behaviors
  • Robot posture selects the expert pool and conditions a shared discriminator with two behavior-specific outputs
  • Task rewards and shared regularization support command tracking and recovery
  • Temporary assistance facilitates exploration during training
  • Simulation-based refinement stage supplies robot-executed motion references for supervision
  • Ablations examine conditional supervision, output separation, and reference quality under matched settings

⚙️ Key details

Capability Result
Independent get-up success 96.80%
Push-recovery success (with command resumption) 96.96%
Torso planar velocity RMSE 0.1266 m/s
Improvement over conditional single-output variant 14.7% lower RMSE
Joint-angle discrepancy (dynamic time warping) Similar to variant
  • Achieves walking, running, get-up, and locomotion resumption after falls
  • Operates with one proprioceptive actor — no controller switching
  • Requires no on-robot policy fine-tuning

🚀 Availability

  • Paper available via arXiv (PDF and experimental HTML views)
  • Associated code and media linked through alphaXiv, CatalyzeX, DagsHub, Gotit.pub, Hugging Face, and ScienceCast
  • Demos referenced in paper metadata

💡 Why it matters

ReLoco demonstrates that a single learned policy can unify continuous locomotion and discrete fall recovery — traditionally handled by separate controllers — while transferring from simulation to a physical 64.5-kg humanoid without additional tuning. The behavior-conditioned adversarial motion prior structure and simulation-based refinement stage provide a template for learning diverse, contact-rich behaviors under a shared architecture.

#Robotics #Humanoid #Locomotion #FallRecovery #ReinforcementLearning #Sim2Real

Source: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors

item.title: XMimic Trains Humanoid Motion Tracking 3.7x Faster Than BlinkMimic
item.description:
XMimic Trains Humanoid Motion Tracking 3.7x Faster Than BlinkMimic

🚀 Overview

XMimic is a new AI development that trains whole-body motion tracking for the Unitree G1 robot 3.7 times faster than the previous BlinkMimic method when using four H100 GPUs. The improvement comes from rebuilding BlinkMimic’s world-model trainer in JAX, enabling faster training while maintaining the same quality.

🧩 How it works

XMimic implements the same algorithm as BlinkMimic but runs entirely in JAX. This includes the simulator (MuJoCo Warp through MJX), the replay buffer, the world model, the policy and the critic. The entire training iterations compile into single XLA programs, so the GPU never waits for Python. The system can distribute iterations across 2 to 4 GPUs working simultaneously.

⚙️ Key details

  • Speed: Reaches BlinkMimic’s target in 0.86 minutes on four H100s (vs. 3.19 minutes on one); on a single H100, XMimic is 1.3 times faster
  • Quality: Both methods achieve the same normalized evaluation return (0.86–0.87) with no clip failures after 6 minutes of training
  • Target: Normalized evaluation return ≥ 0.82 with none of the 40 LAFAN1 clips failing, held for three consecutive checkpoints
  • GPU usage: Uses slightly more total GPU time (3.4 vs. 3.2 GPU-minutes) but the speedup buys wall-clock time
  • Hardware: One H100 NVL per GPU, GPUs connected by NVLink in a node
  • Training: All methods ran on the same cluster; every 100th checkpoint is evaluated on all 40 clips with 4 replicas each
  • Hyperparameters: Uses BlinkMimic’s hyperparameters (PRESET[main], commit d264658)

The development is detailed in the paper XMimic and XSoma: Learning Humanoid Motion Tracking and Locomotion in Under a Minute by Nico Bohlinger and Jan Peters (2026).

📄 Availability

XMimic replaces the first version which covered XMimic alone. It is accompanied by XSoma, which applies the same recipe for locomotion on rough terrain. Please cite the paper if you use XMimic:

XMimic and XSoma: Learning Humanoid Motion Tracking and Locomotion in Under a Minute (Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters, 2026)

#AI #Robotics #JAX #MotionTracking #Humanoid

Source: nico-bohlinger/xmimic
